t: 5.2: Unit Circle - Sine and Cosine Functions - Mathematics LibreTexts
s: May 2, 2022 - More precisely, the sine of an angle \(t\) equals the \(y\)-value of the endpoint on the unit circle of an arc of length \(t\). In Figure \(\PageIndex{3}\), the sine is equal to \(y\). Like all functions, the sine function has an input and an output. Its input is the measure of the angle; its output is the \(y\)-coordinate of the corresponding point on the unit circle. The cosine function of an angle \(t\) equals the \(x\)-value of the endpoint on the unit circle of an arc of length \(t\).

s: The triangle's hypotenuse has length 1, and so (conveniently!) the ratio of its adjacent to its hypotenuse is cos(θ), and the ratio of its opposite to the hypotenuse is sin(θ). Therefore, by placing triangles at the point (0,0) of the x/y plane, the functions sin(θ) and cos(θ) can be found by recording the values of x and y for every θ.
